audit_findings.title: The equity bridge may omit the unpaid $77.3 million PCL claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $79.6 million filed liability at June 30, 2026, equal to a computed $4.05 per fully diluted share and 57.6% of the $138.261 million cash bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: The unpaid judgment and accrued interest are claims ahead of common equity and must reduce the equity bridge once if they are not funded within forecast owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company has $ 77.3 million in liability related to the PCL litigation, which are presented in balance sheet as following: $ 47.0 million in Construction accounts payable and $ 30.3 million in Accounts payable.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission, not merely a possibility. The latest 10-Q reports that the liability remained outstanding at the bridge date and had increased from $77.3 million to $79.6 million. The valuation adds all June cash while deducting none of this liability, materially overstating each per-share value and the buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $79.6 million liability to judgment principal, accrued interest, payments, tax effects and any restricted appeal-bond collateral, then rerun every scenario with the confirmed net common-equity deduction exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The full cash balance may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Any required operating, cage, regulatory or restricted cash is not excess cash and therefore must be excluded from the equity bridge rather than added to operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Funds deposited by customers in advance and outstanding chips and slot tickets in the customers’ possession are recognized as a liability until such amounts are redeemed or used in gaming play by the customer.
audit_findings.explanation: The record establishes $15.516 million of customer-related contractual liabilities at June 30, 2026, including $7.530 million of players-club obligations, $1.633 million of outstanding chips and $6.353 million of customer advances. It does not establish how much cash must be retained against those obligations or for normal casino operations, so the bridge risk is real but its materiality cannot yet be measured. The contractual-liability balance itself is not automatically a dollar-for-dollar cash deduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30 cash-location schedule and management or regulatory minimum-liquidity requirements; identify cage cash, customer-fund coverage, restricted cash and appeal-bond collateral; then rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital may be underidentified within renovations and gaming-equipment spending
audit_findings.mechanism: Understated recurring maintenance capital directly overstates the $105.2 million owner-earnings anchor and every projected annual cash flow and terminal value derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, capital expenditures related primarily to the redesign and upgrade of all hotel rooms at Atlantis, properties maintenance capital expenditures and the acquisition of gaming equipment at both of our properties.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings show $37.216 million of 2025 capital expenditures, $54.022 million of 2025 depreciation and $12.6 million of cash capital spending in the first half of 2026, but they do not separate maintenance from discretionary enhancement spending. Because room redesigns, property enhancements and gaming-equipment replacement can be recurring requirements, the adequacy of the anchor deduction remains unresolved and potentially valuation-relevant.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor's maintenance-capex deduction to project-level invoices and fixed-asset categories, build normalized replacement cycles for rooms and gaming equipment, compare the result with long-run depreciation and total capex, and rerun all scenarios if normalized maintenance differs from the existing deduction.

audit_findings.title: The litigation bucket mixes one-offs with costs that continue until resolution
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.2 million filed 2025 bucket: $3.9 million class-action settlement, $2.7 million judgment interest, $2.4 million appeal fees and $0.2 million other items; valuation treatment unestablished
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining settled one-time charges understates normalized owner earnings, while removing continuing judgment interest and appeal costs overstates owner earnings; unpaid accrued amounts also belong in the bridge if not otherwise captured.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, Other operating items, net was $ 9.2 million and included: $ 2.7 million in accrued interest expense relating to the principal judgment on the litigation between the Company and Monarch Black Hawk’s general contractor, PCL Construction Services, Inc.; $ 2.4 million in professional service fees relating to appeal of the principal judgment on the same litigation; $ 3.9 million in joint stipulation of settlement filed with court in a class action case in which the Company is a defendant; $ 0.1 million in lobbying and other expense to oppose the expansion of iGaming; and $ 0.1 million in loss on disposal of assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The different components require separate treatment. The 2026 filing demonstrates that PCL-related costs continued, with $2.2 million of judgment interest and $0.8 million of litigation professional fees in the first six months. However, the record does not disclose how the $105.2 million anchor treated any 2025 component, so neither the net direction nor valuation materiality can be established.
audit_findings.action: Provide the anchor reconciliation by litigation component; normalize only the demonstrably settled $3.9 million item, retain expected interest and legal costs through resolution, reconcile accrued amounts to the bridge, and rerun the valuation to eliminate both omission and double counting.
